messages:
oncall-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: P1 - multi-region traffic shift detected. Primary->secondary failover in eu-west triggered; automatic traffic-shift job started. Link: https://redwood.incidents/4023456789 :rotating_light:

alex: seeing 5xx spike from customers hitting eu-west endpoints starting ~4023456760. Dashboard: per-route error rate 4.8% -> 12% on some routes. Latency + tail latencies up.

maria: confirming. Synthetic checks show DNS answers inconsistent across resolvers — some regions still resolving to old-eu-hosts, others to new-failover hosts.

kevin: I kicked off a quick dig across public resolvers, pasted below. Looks like route53 weight change + some caches still returning old values.

kevin: ```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.com. 60 IN A 54.23.11.12  ; eu-west primary
api.redwood-inference.com. 60 IN A 3.120.45.8   ; eu-north failover
;; some resolvers return only the failover IP, others return both, TTL still 60
```

samir: also seeing abnormal health-check churn at the cloud LB layer in eu-west zone B — backends flapping Unhealthy->Healthy every ~20s. Could be ongoing drain script that didn't finish and is re-registering.

tara: did we run the traffic-shift job manually for the planned DR test earlier? I recall a canary started at 11:00UTC and was scheduled to finish at 11:20UTC.

alex: yes, the canary job ran but the final step was a controlled weight flip to the failover pool. It seems a subsequent autoscaling/health-recovery process reintroduced some primary IPs into DNS rotation mid-shift, causing a split-brain DNS state.

netops-bot: ALERT: Route53 change detected (change-id Z3XYZ). Change: weighted-record update for api.redwood-inference.com. Source: automation/traffic-shift-job.

maria: customer impact so far: hosted API latency increased for multi-region customers hitting eu endpoints; Dedicated pools with pinned IPs mostly stable. Estimating ~15% of traffic saw degraded responses in the 30m window.

kevin: mitigation plan suggestion: 1) pause traffic-shift automation 2) set explicit weighted record to 100% primary (rollback) or 100% failover depending on ops decision 3) flush CDN / edge caches where possible 4) force health-check stabilization at LB by draining and re-registering backends cleanly.

samir: agree. I'm going to pause the automation job now and put the canary into manual so nothing else makes changes.

samir: /svcctl traffic-shift pause --job-id 2026-DR-11 ; result: OK.

tara: I can push a rollback to 100% primary weight. Suggest we revert to primary while we investigate why the drain didn't complete. Any objections?

alex: rollback sounds right — customers already seeing mixed answers. If we flip back, TTL=60 means some clients will still use failover IP briefly, but it should converge.

kevin: doing rollback. route53 change in flight:```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","Weight":1,"SetIdentifier":"primary-eu-west","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"54.23.11.12"}]}}]}'
```

kevin: change submitted (change-id Z3XYZ-rollback). netops-bot: please monitor propagation.

netops-bot: Route53 change accepted. Status: PENDING.

maria: meanwhile I'm opening a support ticket with the cloud LB team — health-check churn suggests backends rejoined mid-drain, probably due to automated instance reprovisioning. Ticket link: https://cloud.provider/support/CASE-9987

samir: walked the LB logs — I see a race: drain script marked instance OutOfService, automation scaled a replacement which ended up in the old registered pool, then the health-check flapped and we had a mixed state. Fix is to change the automation to respect 'drain in progress' flag.

julia: taking over oncall now for next 2 hours. Julia here — brief me on actions I should continue? :wave:

alex: hey @julia — current state: traffic-shift job paused, route53 rolled back to primary, cloud LB ticket opened, monitoring shows error rate trending down from 12% to ~3% over last 3m. Need to watch residual DNS cache effects and LB health-check stabilization.

julia: ack. I'll keep watching dashboards, stay on this thread. Who owns postmortem?

tara: ops will draft initial incident timeline, SRE + NetOps to own RCA. I'll include the automation owner to update the traffic-shift job to check drain locks.

kevin: small follow-up: CDN edge caches still serving failover IP in a handful of POPs; pushing a purge for api.redwood-inference.com path prefixes now.

kevin: ```
cdnctl purge --pattern "api.redwood-inference.com/*" --regions eu*
```

netops-bot: CDN purge acknowledged.

maria: customer-facing note: prepare a short blurb — Hosted API customers may have seen increased errors & latency between 11:10-11:40UTC in EU; Dedicated customers with pinned endpoints mostly unaffected. No data loss. ETA for stabilization: monitoring for next 30m.

julia: drafting blurb and will post to status.redwood shortly.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: @alex handing to @julia for next shift (11:45UTC). PagerDuty incident remains open.

alex: @julia — if error rate climbs back above 5% escalate and we'll re-open automation in safe-mode if needed.

samir: temporary mitigation complete. Long-term actions I recommend: (1) add drain-in-progress lock to autoscaler/replace flow, (2) add a sanity check before weighted DNS flips (verify LB HC stable for N minutes), (3) reduce TTL during DR runs to minimize cache split windows, (4) add canary-based end-to-end check that validates consistent DNS answers from multiple global resolvers.

tara: adding action items to triage board now.

maria: final status update: error rates back to baseline ~1% across EU. Route53 change propagated. LB health-check stable. Customer impact: degraded responses for ~15% of EU traffic for ~30 minutes. No customer data loss.

julia: closing loop: I'll own post-incident follow-up and confirm owners for the four recommended action items. Posting status update to #status and notifying support. Good job everyone. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity reduced to SEV-RESOLVED. Incident will remain open for RCA tracking.
